newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian base metals steady on limited arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian base metals steady on limited arrivals.

text.p: Base metals remained steady at the improved level on the local market, dealers said on Wednesday.
Demand from industrial consumers remained negligible but an upsurge in the world market and limited arrivals kept local offerings at a low ebb.
"Ready copper was steady at 13,600 rupees per quintal amid poor activity but undercurrent was firm on reports of rising world prices," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metals Exchange.
"Copper prices here may move up again if demand comes in."
Other base metals remained steady at the previous level in nominal activity as physical enquiries stayed sluggish.

Zinc was quiet at 7,950 rupees, as was lead at 4,150 rupees and aluminium at 7,950 rupees per quintal. Nickel was steady at 36,900 rupees after a gain of 100 rupees per quintal on Tuesday while tin was indicated at the previous level of 31,200 rupees per quintal amid nominal trading.

"Physical activity in the Bombay market remained at a low ebb amid absence of fresh enquiries from the industrial buyers but looking at the upsurge in the world market local prices may bounce back again," Parikh added.
